rights.text_basis: First published 1582 and 1610. Long out of copyright everywhere.

TIT.1.1.text: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of the elect of God and the acknowledging of the truth, which is according to godliness:

TIT.1.2.text: Unto the hope of life everlasting, which God, who lieth not, hath promised before the times of the world:

TIT.1.3.text: But hath in due times manifested his word in preaching, which is committed to me according to the commandment of God our Saviour:

TIT.1.4.text: To Titus my beloved son, according to the common faith, grace and peace from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus our Saviour.

TIT.1.5.text: For this cause I left thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and shouldest ordain priests in every city, as I also appointed thee:

TIT.1.6.text: If any be without crime, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, not accused of riot, or unruly.

TIT.1.7.text: For a bishop must be without crime, as the steward of God: not proud, not subject to anger, not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre:

TIT.1.8.text: But given to hospitality, gentle, sober, just, holy, continent:

TIT.1.9.text: Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine, that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine, and to convince the gainsayers.

TIT.1.10.text: For there are also many disobedient, vain talkers, and seducers: especially they who are of the circumcision:

TIT.1.11.text: Who must be reproved, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.

TIT.1.12.text: One of them a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are always liars, evil beasts, slothful bellies.

TIT.1.13.text: This testimony is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;

TIT.1.14.text: Not giving heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men, who turn themselves away from the truth.

TIT.1.15.text: All things are clean to the clean: but to them that are defiled, and to unbelievers, nothing is clean: but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.

TIT.1.16.text: They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him; being abominable, and incredulous, and to every good work reprobate.

TIT.2.1.text: But speak thou the things that become sound doctrine:

TIT.2.2.text: That the aged men be sober, chaste, prudent, sound in faith, in love in patience.

TIT.2.3.text: The aged women, in like manner, in holy attire, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teaching well:

TIT.2.4.text: That they may teach the young women to be wise, to love their husbands, to love their children,

TIT.2.5.text: To be discreet, chaste, sober, having a care of the house, gentle, obedient to their husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.

TIT.2.6.text: Young men, in like manner, exhort that they be sober.

TIT.2.7.text: In all things shew thyself an example of good works, in doctrine, in integrity, in gravity,

TIT.2.8.text: The sound word that can not be blamed: that he, who is on the contrary part, may be afraid, having no evil to say of us.

TIT.2.9.text: Exhort servants to be obedient to their masters, in all things pleasing, not gainsaying:

TIT.2.10.text: Not defrauding, but in all things shewing good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things:

TIT.2.11.text: For the grace of God our Saviour hath appeared to all men;

TIT.2.12.text: Instructing us, that, denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, and justly, and godly in this world,

TIT.2.13.text: Looking for the blessed hope and coming of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ,

TIT.2.14.text: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and might cleanse to himself a people acceptable, a pursuer of good works.

TIT.2.15.text: These things speak, and exhort and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

TIT.3.1.text: Admonish them to be subject to princes and powers, to obey at a word, to be ready to every good work.

TIT.3.2.text: To speak evil of no man, not to be litigious, but gentle: shewing all mildness towards all men.

TIT.3.3.text: For we ourselves also were some time unwise, incredulous, erring, slaves to divers desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.

TIT.3.4.text: But when the goodness and kindness of God our Saviour appeared:

TIT.3.5.text: Not by the works of justice, which we have done, but according to his mercy, he saved us, by the laver of regeneration, and renovation of the Holy Ghost;

TIT.3.6.text: Whom he hath poured forth upon us abundantly, through Jesus Christ our Saviour:

TIT.3.7.text: That, being justified by his grace, we may be heirs, according to hope of life everlasting.

TIT.3.8.text: It is a faithful saying: and these things I will have thee affirm constantly: that they, who believe in God, may be careful to excel in good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

TIT.3.9.text: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law. For they are unprofitable and vain.

TIT.3.10.text: A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid:

TIT.3.11.text: Knowing that he, that is such an one, is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned by his own judgment.

TIT.3.12.text: When I shall send to thee Artemas or Tychicus, make haste to come unto me to Nicopolis. For there I have determined to winter.

TIT.3.13.text: Send forward Zenas, the lawyer, and Apollo, with care, that nothing be wanting to them.

TIT.3.14.text: And let our men also learn to excel in good works for necessary uses: that they be not unfruitful.

TIT.3.15.text: All that are with me salute thee: salute them that love us in the faith. The grace of God be with you all. Amen.
